bugs: The job's idempotency guard reads the model state from when the job was deserialized (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:56 `$this->event->status === Processed`), not a fresh conditional claim. A duplicate job that deserialized before the first job finished will process the event again: it calls the provider again and applies the side effects again. A probe confirmed this. The order transitions limit the damage, but the event can still be processed twice.
failed() calls markFailed unconditionally (app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:62), so a late or duplicate failure overwrites an event that is already Processed and sets it to Failed. A probe confirmed this.

The payment API is called before the order lookup (Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:70-72, the order is fetched inside apply()). Events for unknown orders therefore use up a rate-limited provider request before they fail permanently.
The X-Signature check is case-sensitive, so a valid uppercase hex signature gets a 401.
An event with an empty `data` object gets a 422, even for unknown event types.
antipatterns: app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:12 implements both ShouldQueue and ShouldQueueAfterCommit. This is redundant because ShouldQueueAfterCommit already extends ShouldQueue.

app/Console/Commands/RedispatchStuckWebhookEvents.php plus its five-minute schedule (routes/console.php:13) add a recovery mechanism the task did not ask for. It has its own scope, constant coupling (RETRY_WINDOW_MINUTES + 30) and README section.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:98 validates payload data inside the job with Validator::make, instead of validating type-specific fields at ingestion in the FormRequest.
app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:47-64 uses forceFill/save for status writes, with no guard on the current state.
strengths: Uses createOrFirst on a unique event_id and dispatches only when wasRecentlyCreated, so the controller is thin.
The job uses WithoutOverlapping, RateLimited with a named limiter (Limit::perSecond(10)), Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout attributes and retryUntil, and it handles 429, 5xx and 4xx separately.
Order state changes use conditional updates (transitionTo), which prevents downgrades and duplicate receipts.
The receipt notification is queued with ShouldQueueAfterCommit inside the transaction.
Uses MassPrunable with a daily scheduled model:prune.
Has the strongest tests, including one that runs the real RateLimited middleware and checks that 10 jobs pass and 2 are released, an HTTP-to-queue end-to-end test, and 429/5xx/connection/4xx paths.
The README covers worker deployment in detail (Supervisor, retry_after vs timeout, shared cache, queue:restart).
Correctly makes webhooks/* render JSON exceptions.

bugs: bootstrap/app.php does not make webhooks/* render JSON exceptions. A signed webhook that fails validation and has no Accept: application/json header gets a 302 redirect instead of 422. A probe confirmed this. Providers will see a redirect and may retry it indefinitely.

If the provider response has no `amount` key, `(int) $details['amount']` (Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:78) throws an ErrorException. This counts as a transient failure and is retried up to MaxExceptions before the event is marked failed, so a permanent data error is treated as transient.
An event with an empty `data` object is rejected with a validation error, even for unknown event types.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:78 `markPaid(...) && $order->user->notify(...)` uses a short-circuit expression inside a match arm for a side effect (notify returns void), which is clever but obscure.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:56 hardcodes the handled-type list in the job, and StoreWebhookEventRequest repeats it as a comma-separated string constant.
The Backoff attribute plus retryUntil of 2 hours, with the explanatory docblock, is slightly heavier than needed.
strengths: WebhookEvent::claim() is an atomic conditional update that re-reads state, so stale or duplicate jobs never re-process an event that is already Processed or Failed. A probe confirmed this.
markFailed is guarded so a late failed() cannot overwrite Processed (and this is tested).
Looks up the order before calling the provider, so it does not spend rate-limited API calls on unknown orders.
Validates type-specific fields at ingestion with required_if in the FormRequest, and the index request has typed status()/perPage() helpers using $request->enum().
Uses modern attributes throughout (Backoff, MaxExceptions, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels, Tries on the notification, #[Scope], #[Fillable]), plus the Queueable from Foundation.
The receipt uses ShouldQueueAfterCommit and is sent inside a DB transaction, and refunds use createOrFirst on a unique provider_refund_id.
The prune schedule uses onOneServer, and the README explains the shared cache, retry_after vs timeout and Supervisor config.
Signature comparison is case-insensitive and constant-time, and fails closed when no secret is configured.

v.rationale:
Both implementations follow nearly the same design: createOrFirst ingestion, a signature middleware, a job with WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited, a named 10/s limiter, Backoff/MaxExceptions/retryUntil attributes, conditional order transitions, a ShouldQueueAfterCommit receipt, MassPrunable with a daily model:prune, and an admin index protected by a policy over auth.basic. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 37 tests, impl-1: 42 tests).

The deciding difference is how each one guards against processing an event twice. impl-2 claims the event with an atomic conditional UPDATE and a refresh, and markFailed will not overwrite a Processed event. In probes it skipped a stale job without calling the provider. impl-1 checks the status on the model as it was when the job was deserialized. In probes it re-ran the provider call and the side effects for an event that was already processed, and its failed() changed a Processed event to Failed. impl-1 also calls the provider before looking up the order, and it adds an extra redispatch-stuck command and schedule the task did not ask for.

impl-2's real bug is that webhooks/* does not render JSON exceptions, so a validation failure without an Accept header returns a 302. This is less severe than impl-1's idempotency gaps. impl-1 has the better tests (a real rate-limiter behaviour test and an HTTP-to-queue end-to-end test), but that does not outweigh its correctness problems in the task's focus area. impl-2 ranks first.
